subsystems.name: Mode-locked laser
subsystems.role: generates the train of evenly spaced optical frequencies that form the comb.

subsystems.name: Frequency stabilization
subsystems.role: locks the comb's spacing and offset to a stable reference so its absolute wavelengths are known.

subsystems.name: Spectral broadening and filtering
subsystems.role: extends the comb across the spectrograph's band and matches line spacing to its resolution.

subsystems.name: Delivery and scrambling
subsystems.role: brings the comb light to the spectrograph with the same beam geometry as starlight.

subsystems.name: Calibration and analysis
subsystems.role: compares starlight positions with comb lines to measure wavelength shifts.

buildSteps.title: Build the laser
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a mode-locked laser — typically erbium fiber or titanium-sapphire — that emits a train of ultrashort pulses, producing thousands of evenly spaced optical frequencies.

buildSteps.title: Lock the repetition rate
buildSteps.detail: Stabilize the pulse repetition rate to an atomic clock, GPS signal or stable cavity so the comb spacing is known.

buildSteps.title: Lock the carrier-envelope offset
buildSteps.detail: Measure the offset frequency with an f-2f interferometer and feed it back to control electronics, anchoring every comb line absolutely.

buildSteps.title: Amplify and broaden
buildSteps.detail: Boost the pulses and pass them through nonlinear optical fiber to spread the comb across the full wavelength range the spectrograph observes.

buildSteps.title: Filter the comb
buildSteps.detail: Use a Fabry-Perot cavity or etalon to select lines at the spectrograph's resolution, preventing line blending.

buildSteps.title: Couple to the spectrograph
buildSteps.detail: Inject the comb light through the same optical fiber as starlight, ensuring it takes the identical path so any instrumental drift affects both equally.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and validate
buildSteps.detail: Record the comb lines, compare them against known wavelengths, and then interleave comb exposures with starlight during observations.

buildSteps.title: Operate and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Continuously track drift, correct the stellar spectrum against the comb, and flag any loss of lock.

prerequisites.why: they produce the stable, evenly spaced optical frequencies that form the comb.
techniques such as f-2f interferometry and phase locking are needed to anchor the comb to an absolute reference.
they resolve individual comb lines and provide the dispersion needed for precise radial-velocity measurements.
they broaden the comb to cover the visible or near-infrared band of the spectrograph.
atomic clocks or GPS-disciplined oscillators keep the comb's absolute wavelengths stable over long campaigns.
